text:
Jonesboro-Hodge Middle School enrolls 152 students in 2025-26 school year
G. A. Mcgill
Jonesboro-Hodge Middle School had 152 students enrolled in the 2025-26 school year, according to the Louisiana Department of Education.
Enrollment rose 3.4% from the previous school year, when the school enrolled 147 students.
In the 2025-26 school year, 52.6% of students were boys and 47.4% were girls.
Black students were the largest group, making up 65.1% of Jonesboro-Hodge Middle School's total enrollment.
The school is in Jackson Parish School District, which has its central office in Jonesboro.
Statewide, Louisiana enrolled 660,349 students in the 2025-26 school year.
Louisiana ranked near the bottom nationally for public school systems, according to WalletHub's 2026 analysis. The state ranked 44th among the 50 states and Washington, D.C., with a quality rank of 42 and a safety rank of 48. WalletHub's analysis compared states across 32 metrics, including measures tied to student performance, funding, school safety, class size and instructor credentials.
Black and white students were the two largest groups reported in Louisiana public schools in 2025, according to KIDS COUNT data from Agenda for Children based on Louisiana Department of Education enrollment figures. Black students made up 41.8% of public school enrollment, while white students accounted for 40.2%. Hispanic students accounted for 11.6% of enrollment, continuing a long-term increase in the state's public schools.
Information in this article was obtained from the Kentucky Department of Education. The source data can be found here.
